To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a model that assumes heterogeneity in a population is a better explanation of our data than a homogeneous population model, and (ii) the model that assumes individual differences is especially better at explaining the comprehension data than the homogeneous population model.

a) the population of speakers is not homogeneous with respect to the depth of pragmatic reasoning, and b) probabilistic modeling of pragmatic inference is a useful tool to study individual differences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to integrate individual differences into probabilistic models of pragmatic reasoning.
the role of individual differences in pragmatic inference.
the question whether the probabilistic modeling of language use is compatible with the existence of individual differences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are individual differences in the ability to make inferences about the speaker’s intentions.
probabilistic pragmatic models are a good starting point to understand the mechanisms of pragmatic inference, but that they need to be extended to include individual differences.
the probabilistic models of reference games are a good approximation of the data, but that they should be extended to allow for individual differences in the population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that a model that allows for individual differences in pragmatic reasoning is more successful than a model that does not allow for individual differences in predicting the data.
the probabilistic modeling of language use should take into account both population level and individual level differences.
the individual differences in pragmatic reasoning are more complex than previously assumed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
probabilistic pragmatic models can be used to model individual speakers' and listeners’ pragmatic reasoning in reference games.
individual differences in reasoning are important to account for, and that probabilistic models are a promising way of doing so.
the population level models of pragmatic reasoning should not be interpreted as a homogeneous population without any individual differences.
